cover letter

01. The information provided in your application must support your selected answers in the supplemental questions. The information you provide will be verified and documentation may be required. Please be as honest and accurate as possible. You may be asked to demonstrate your knowledge and skills in a work sample or during an interview. By completing this supplemental questionnaire you are attesting that the information you have provided is accurate. Any misstatements, omissions, or falsification of information may eliminate you from consideration. Options: Yes, I understand and agree

02. Which statement below best describes the highest level of education you have completed? Options: Some High School | High school graduate, diploma or the equivalent (GED) | Some college (less than 60 units) | Associate degree or at least 60 semester units | Bachelor's degree | Master's degree | Professional degree | Doctorate degree | None of the above
03. Do you have a Bachelor's degree or higher in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, Public Administration or a closely related field? Options: Yes | No

04. Select all that you currently hold. Select all that apply. Options: California Chief Business Official (CBO) certification | Certified Public Accountant (CPA) | Certified Management Accountant (CMA) | Currently enrolled in a CBO certification program | None of the above
05. List any additional certifications, licenses, or professional credentials you hold, including the issuing organization and expiration date (if applicable). Enter "N/A" if none apply.

06. How many years of management experience do you have in business, fiscal, or financial management services in a public agency? Options: No experience | Less than 3 years | 3 years but less than 4 years | 4 years but less than 5 years | 5 years but less than 8 years | 8 years or more

07. How many years of that experience included management responsibility for MORE THAN ONE functional areas — such as fiscal services, purchasing, facilities, maintenance and operations, transportation, technology, food services, or risk management — including supervision of professional, supervisory, or management-level staff? Options: No experience | Less than 1 year | 1 year but less than 2 years | 2 years but less than 3 years | 3 years but less than 5 years | 5 years or more

08. Which statement best describes your highest level of management responsibility? Select the option that best describes the full scope of your experience. Options: I performed professional or technical fiscal or business work as an individual contributor. | I supervised staff within a single fiscal or business function. | I managed one (1) fiscal or business department, directing work through supervisors or lead staff. | I managed two (2) or more distinct departments or functional areas through subordinate supervisors or managers. | I held agency-wide executive responsibility for fiscal and operational services, reporting directly to a superintendent, chief executive, or governing board.

09. Select all operational (non-fiscal) functions for which you have held direct management or oversight responsibility. Select all that apply. Options: Maintenance, operations, or custodial services | Facilities planning, construction, or capital projects | Pupil or fleet transportation | Information technology | Food or nutrition services | Purchasing, warehouse, or distribution | Risk management, insurance, or workers' compensation | Other | None of the above

10. Which setting best describes where you gained the majority of your qualifying management experience? Options: Private sector or non-profit | Public agency other than education (city, county, special district, or state) | County office of education, community college, or other public education agency | California K-12 school district | Other

11. Based on your business, fiscal, or operational management experience, please provide details for your MOST RELEVANT positions, beginning with the most recent. For each position, include: (a) Job Title: (b) Organization/Agency Name: (c) Type of Agency (California K-12 school district, county office of education, community college, other public agency, private, or non-profit): (d) Title of the Position You Reported To: (e) Functions or Departments You Managed (for example, fiscal services, purchasing, facilities, maintenance and operations, transportation, technology, food services, or risk management, (if any)): (f) Classification Titles and Number of Staff Reporting to You, Directly and Through Subordinates: (g) Approximate Annual Operating Budget You Were Accountable For: (h) Employment Period: (From MM/YYYY to MM/YYYY) If you have no relevant experience in this area, enter "N/A."

12. In 250 words or less, describe a budget, interim report, or multiyear projection you personally prepared or certified that identified an ongoing shortfall, and what you recommended to close it. Include: • Organization, fiscal year, and total budget size • What you personally produced, versus what staff produced • The most difficult assumption you had to make, how you supported it, and whether any external reviewer questioned it • Size of the shortfall, in dollars and as a percentage of the budget • What you specifically recommended, and what you chose to protect • The outcome, including the effect on fund balance If you have not personally held this responsibility, describe your closest related experience, then explain how you would approach identifying and closing an ongoing budget shortfall.

13. In 250 words or less, describe your experience with facilities capital projects or a voter-approved bond program. Include: • Organization and total program or project value • Your specific role and what you were accountable for • Funding sources involved • How you tracked expenditures and ensured compliance • One problem you resolved - cost, schedule, scope, or audit finding If your capital experience is limited, describe your experience managing restricted funds subject to external audit, then explain how you would approach establishing fiscal oversight of a large capital program.
Directs the District's fiscal, business, and operational services, aligning departmental goals, staffing, and resources with District-wide priorities and performance objectives.

Directs and evaluates the performance of subordinate directors and assigned managerial staff; establishes goals, performance expectations, and accountability measures for assigned functions; interviews and selects employees; recommends disciplinary actions; and arranges for training and development of subordinates.

Advises the Superintendent regarding use of resources, priorities, program opportunities, and methods to enhance the delivery of programs and support services; serves as the Superintendent's designee for assigned fiscal, business, and operational matters.

Directs financial and strategic planning, budget development, and fund allocation, including fiscal alignment of the Local Control and Accountability Plan (LCAP) with Local Control Funding Formula (LCFF) requirements; conducts financial and statistical studies to project, upgrade, or evaluate programs and services.

Directs the preparation and certification of the annual budget, interim financial reports, and multiyear financial projections in accordance with state fiscal accountability and oversight requirements; oversees attendance and enrollment reporting to ensure accuracy of apportionment claims; and prepares required public disclosures of the costs of collective bargaining agreements.

Directs enrollment forecasting and long-range fiscal planning; analyzes the fiscal impact of enrollment, attendance, and revenue trends and the encroachment of restricted programs on unrestricted resources; and develops resource allocation, expenditure reduction, and organizational realignment strategies to maintain long-term fiscal solvency.

Directs District fiscal services, including fiscal reporting, revenue collection and disbursement functions, cash management and cash flow projection, accounting, payroll and retirement systems and records, categorical and grant program fiscal compliance, auditing programs, and warrant issuance and commercial claims processing in accordance with County financial reporting and compliance requirements.

Directs the annual independent audit, including preparation of financial statements, response to audit findings, and implementation of corrective actions; oversees associated student body, student activity, and other agency fund accounting and control.

Directs the administration, implementation, and conversion of the District's enterprise resource planning (ERP) and integrated financial, budget, payroll, and human capital management systems, including coordination with the County Office of Education on countywide system requirements, conversion schedules, and reporting standards.
Establishes and oversees systems of internal control across assigned functions; evaluates adherence to statutory requirements, legal mandates, and District regulatory protocols.

Directs facilities master planning and capital programs, including needs assessment, project prioritization, capital improvement, construction, and modernization projects aligned with District enrollment and budgetary priorities.

Directs capital and long-term financing, including general obligation bond programs, debt issuance and administration, developer fees, and state facilities funding applications; oversees expenditure tracking, performance and financial audits, and support to the citizens' bond oversight committee.

Directs the management of District real property, including surplus property evaluation and disposition, joint-use and lease agreements, and property-related revenue, in accordance with statutory requirements.

Directs the District's operational services, including maintenance and operations services; pupil transportation services; information technology services, including infrastructure, enterprise systems, and data security; and food services, including operations, fund solvency, and compliance with state and federal child nutrition requirements.

Directs the District's contract administration and purchasing services, including competitive bidding, review, negotiation, and approval of contracts and agreements, vendor administration, warehouse and distribution operations, and inventory control, ensuring compliance with public contracting laws and Board policy.

Directs the District's risk management program, including property, liability, and workers' compensation coverage and claims administration; evaluates and recommends insurance and self-insurance strategies; coordinates with third-party administrators, legal counsel, and joint powers authorities; and monitors claims experience, reserves, and loss trends to protect District assets and minimize financial exposure.

Oversees District loss prevention and occupational safety programs, including the Injury and Illness Prevention Program, safety training, and compliance with Cal/OSHA and environmental regulatory requirements.
Reports to the Board of Education on District fiscal, business, and operational matters, including the annual budget, budget status, and program performance.
Participates in District collective bargaining and advises on the fiscal impacts of proposals.

Represents the District with the County Office of Education, other public agencies and commissions, joint powers authorities, professional associations, and community groups; responds to inquiries and escalations related to audits and reporting; and makes presentations relating to school business and financial management.
Performs related duties as assigned
Principles and practices of public administration, executive leadership, organizational management, and strategic planning
Public sector finance, budgeting, accounting, procurement, contracts, and resource management
Enrollment forecasting, demographic analysis, and long-range fiscal planning, including expenditure reduction and resource realignment strategies
Financial and statistical record-keeping techniques and internal control systems

Enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems and integrated financial, budget, payroll, and human capital management systems, including implementation, conversion, data conversion and integrity, and end-user training practices
Facilities planning, capital projects, and construction and modernization funding, including bonds, federal special funding programs, and grants
Principles and practices of facilities maintenance and operations, pupil transportation, information technology, and food services administration
Principles and practices of collective bargaining, labor relations, and human resources administration
Principles and practices of supervision, staff development, and performance management, including direction exercised through subordinate management staff
Modern office practices and procedures, including enterprise software, infrastructure management, and cybersecurity practices
Governmental accounting standards, the California School Accounting Manual, and the Standardized Account Code Structure (SACS)
Fundamental concepts of employment laws, codes, and regulations, including EEO, FLSA, FMLA, and Cal/OSHA and applicable provisions of collective bargaining agreements
Plan, direct, and integrate complex business, operational, and financial planning, budgeting, and District programs.
Manage organizational change and design organizational structures to maximize the effectiveness of District operations.
Direct the implementation and conversion of enterprise financial and human capital management systems, including planning, resource allocation, staff training, and change management.
Direct multiple functional areas through subordinate management staff and hold them accountable for results.
Plan, track, and evaluate projects to ensure timely completion and alignment with long-range District objectives.
Analyze, interpret, and prepare financial statements, forecasts, and reports.
Analyze demographic, enrollment, and revenue trends and develop long-range plans to sustain fiscal solvency.
Evaluate organizational risk exposure and recommend insurance, self-insurance, and loss prevention strategies to protect District assets.
Prepare and present complex information and recommendations to District administration, the Board of Education, and external stakeholders.
Provide leadership, supervision, and training to a diverse workforce; guide and motivate others toward common goals.
Resolve conflicts and handle sensitive situations with discretion and professionalism.
Collaborate effectively with school administrators, staff, and external agencies.
Work independently while effectively managing competing priorities.
Interpret, apply, and explain applicable laws, codes, rules, and regulations.
Utilize accounting software, financial management systems, and standard office applications.
Model communications and interactions that respect and include all individuals and their languages, abilities, religions, and cultures.

Principles and practices of risk management, including property, liability, and workers' compensation programs, claims administration, self-insurance and joint powers authority participation, loss prevention, and occupational safety programs
Local Control Funding Formula (LCFF) apportionment, Local Control and Accountability Plan (LCAP) fiscal requirements, and categorical and restricted funding compliance
